units.text: He survived an atomic bomb. Three days later, he survived another.
units.phonemes: hiː sɚvˈaɪvd ɐn ɐtˈɑːmɪk bˈɑːm. θɹˈiː dˈeɪz lˈeɪɾɚ, hiː sɚvˈaɪvd ɐnˈʌðɚ.

units.text: This is Tsutomu Yamaguchi, a Mitsubishi shipbuilding engineer.
units.phonemes: ðɪs ɪz tsˈuːɾəmˌuː jˌæmɐɡˈʌtʃi, ɐ mˌɪtsuːbˈiːʃi ʃˈɪpbɪldɪŋ ˌɛndʒɪnˈɪɹ.

units.text: August sixth, nineteen forty-five. He was in Hiroshima on business when the United States dropped an atomic bomb.
units.phonemes: ˈɔːɡəst sˈɪksθ, nˈaɪntiːn fˈɔːɹɾifˈaɪv. hiː wʌz ɪn hˌɪɹəʃˈiːmə ˌɔn bˈɪznəs wɛn ðə juːnˈaɪɾᵻd stˈeɪts dɹˈɑːpt ɐn ɐtˈɑːmɪk bˈɑːm.

units.text: The next day, he boarded a train. It carried him home to Nagasaki.
units.phonemes: ðə nˈɛkst dˈeɪ, hiː bˈoːɹdᵻd ɐ tɹˈeɪn. ɪt kˈæɹid hˌɪm hˈoʊm tə nˌæɡɐsˈæki.

units.text: On August ninth, he was back at work. He recalled describing Hiroshima to his manager.
units.phonemes: ˌɔn ˈɔːɡəst nˈaɪnθ, hiː wʌz bˈæk æt wˈɜːk. hiː ɹᵻkˈɔːld dᵻskɹˈaɪbɪŋ hˌɪɹəʃˈiːmə tə hɪz mˈænɪdʒɚ.

units.text: Then came another flash. The second atomic bomb had struck.
units.phonemes: ðˈɛn kˈeɪm ɐnˈʌðɚ flˈæʃ. ðə sˈɛkənd ɐtˈɑːmɪk bˈɑːm hæd stɹˈʌk.

units.text: He survived again. His wife and infant son survived too.
units.phonemes: hiː sɚvˈaɪvd ɐɡˈɛn. hɪz wˈaɪf ænd ˈɪnfənt sˈʌn sɚvˈaɪvd tˈuː.

units.text: The bombings killed tens of thousands and left lasting suffering.
units.phonemes: ðə bˈɑːmɪŋz kˈɪld tˈɛnz ʌv θˈaʊzəndz ænd lˈɛft lˈæstɪŋ sˈʌfɚɹɪŋ.

units.text: In two thousand nine, Japan officially recognized his exposure in both cities.
units.phonemes: ɪn tˈuː θˈaʊzənd nˈaɪn, dʒəpˈæn əfˈɪʃəli ɹˈɛkəɡnˌaɪzd hɪz ɛkspˈoʊʒɚɹ ɪn bˈoʊθ sˈɪɾiz.

units.text: He was not the only double survivor.
units.phonemes: hiː wʌz nˌɑːt ðɪ ˈoʊnli dˈʌbəl sɚvˈaɪvɚ.

units.text: He lived until twenty ten, aged ninety-three.
units.phonemes: hiː lˈɪvd ʌntˈɪl twˈɛnti tˈɛn, ˈeɪdʒd nˈaɪndiθɹˈiː.

units.text: In later years, he urged the world to abolish nuclear weapons.
units.phonemes: ɪn lˈeɪɾɚ jˈɪɹz, hiː ˈɜːdʒd ðə wˈɜːld tʊ ɐbˈɑːlɪʃ nˈuːklɪɹ wˈɛpənz.
